The payload fixture now hashes the names of the fields a seat's broadcast state carries. Not breaking for built bundles, but a game built on this BoardSmith needs the re-vendored engine: its GameShell reads gameInstanceId, and without it no replacement (undo included) tears down an open pick.
SnapshotSessionHost takes an optional hostWork gate (new HostWorkGate type): demo moves and bot chains wait on it while the host's rules are being replaced; a host without one runs that work at once

WORLD_REFUSALS gains the caller-owned world-ended code, WorldStore gains endedAt() and WorldCheckpointExtras gains endedAt: an ended world's ending is durable, the ending's checkpoint empties the schedule, and ResidentWorld refuses commands with world-ended and runs no events or clock commands after it (#395)

enterText refuses control characters (C0, DEL, C1; a multiline field admits line feed and tab) and unpaired surrogates with a player-facing sentence, takes an optional maxBytes that bounds the UTF-8 bytes the text adds to a partition (measured as the partition store measures), and its pattern is now { regex, message }. The text pick on the wire gains maxBytes (only when set) and carries pattern as { source, message } instead of a bare source string (#394).

chooseFrom, chooseElement and chooseElements (table and world) take an optional unavailable(value, ctx) sentence for a submitted value that is no longer listed; without it the player now reads a plain 'That choice is no longer available... please choose again' instead of the engine's value-and-choices text, which moves to the dev log (#393)

A world action's .quote() and every callback of a pick re-asked with earlier answers bound (prompt, choices/elements, prepare, disabled, multiSelect) now receive each element selection as its read-only element, resolved exactly as dispatch resolves it for execute, instead of the raw id the draft carried (#418). A draft whose element id names nothing the action can offer the seat now (taken since the offer, or never offered) is refused with the new caller-owned refusal code stale-draft; a host relays it on the world_pick / world_quote answer like any other refusal.

A world can leave a lasting NOTICE for a seat without loading that seat's partition (ShufflewickPub #521, BoardSmith #420). world.notices: { perSeat } declares a per-seat notice box, capped by the new budget maxNoticesPerSeat (64); noticeMaxBytes (1024) bounds one notice and maxNoticesPerCommand (100) the sends per dispatch. ctx.world.notify(seat, { payload, line?, whenFull }) appends to a box with no declaration and no partition load; whenFull is required -- 'dropOldest' evicts and counts dropped, 'refuse' refuses the command (notice-box-full) and needs the box declared. .noticeBox(fn) on worldAction and worldClockAction declares ONE seat's box per round of the walk; the host answers a point read and ctx.world.notices(seat) / takeNotices(seat) read it and empty it. WorldDispatchNeeds gains noticeBoxes; runner.declare and commandNeeds take WorldWalkAnswers { declaredActivity, declaredNotices } and walkDeclaration takes a fourth reader and returns that object, which apply takes; WorldCommandStamp, WorldEventStamp and WorldApplyRequest carry declaredNotices; WorldCommandResult carries notices: { perSeat, writes } which a host applies with applyNoticeWrites in the checkpoint's own write, and each send is also a routed event on the reserved scope 'notice' to its one seat. WorldStore gains noticeBox(seat) and WorldCheckpointExtras.notices, and a vacated chair's box goes with it. New refusals: invalid-notice, notice-batch-cap, notice-box-full, undeclared-notice-box (game) and notice-box-answered-wrong (platform); the partition name 'notice' is reserved. formatHash unmoved: no stored partition byte changes.

Bots in hidden-information games (a determinize sampler, such as Go Fish) no longer search moves for a seat that is not to move in the sampled world, and a move the engine refuses during the search is no longer scored as if it had been played, so their searches spend no work on illegal moves (#421). SnapshotSessionHost now holds back a bot seat whose move was refused, or that stalled, until the snapshot changes, and keeps driving the other bot seats instead of stopping the pump. A refused botTurn result now names the seat in botPlayer; the executor must forward botPlayer on its error result for the host to hold back only that seat, otherwise the pump stops as before. GameSession no longer re-checks bots in a loop while a human is to move or after a refused bot move.

Adopts engine changes no fingerprint covers, made since r113 was packed (ShufflewickPub #532): GameShell's game-over card and announcement wait for a board that holds its result back (holdGameOverUntil, useGameOverReveal) and the announcement names the result the card shows (#419); the phone top strip keeps its height when the game ends (#431); providesOwnGameOverUi works when written in kebab-case (#433); boardsmith validate names the engine revision a type error runs into (#423); boardsmith test ends a failed run with a verdict naming the failing files or the signal (#429); test-step-check mutates .vue components (#425); ledger-check and claim-quote-check accept BoardSmith source cited from the installed package and claims quoting code their own chunk replaced (#426, #432). No surface, payload or format change.

boardsmith pack names its tarball after the tree it packs instead of the time it ran: <version>-r<revision>-<content hash>, so packing unchanged sources gives the same file and a no-op re-vendor changes nothing (#434). No engine behaviour changed.

Seats and spectators are sent a PublicFlowState (no moveCount, frame counters, turnRun, followUp or actionError) instead of the server FlowState, and PlayerGameState no longer carries actionCount or turnStartActionIndex (#449).

A player's identity fields (name, $type, seat, color, colorLabel, status) now always reach other seats whatever the Player class's visibleAttributes says, and a whitelist naming one is refused; other elements' whitelists are unchanged (#448)

Table-game element ids are now opaque: Speck32/64 of the creation counter under a 64-bit key the engine mints per game (GameOptions.elementIdKey, recorded in snapshot.gameOptions and never sent to a seat), so a seat cannot count creations hidden from it and a guessable seed does not decode them. A table state restores only into a game built with its key; table snapshots saved before this cannot be restored. World ids are unchanged (#447, #482)

Engine-owned game options (seed, elementIdKey, playerCount, ...) are named once in ENGINE_OWNED_GAME_OPTION_KEYS; boardsmith/session exports selectGameOptions, the one way a client's choice of game options is admitted (declared options only, typed, never a host-owned key), and GameSession, its lobby and the dev host take only such a selection; a start op refuses gameOptions.elementIdKey (#447)

No behaviour change: mintElementIdKey reads crypto by its bare name instead of globalThis.crypto, so boardsmith, boardsmith/session, boardsmith/session-host, boardsmith/world, boardsmith/persistence and boardsmith/runtime typecheck under Cloudflare Workers types (crypto is declared const there). r119 failed the platform's games/ typecheck; adopt this build instead (#488)

Debug ops are refused unless the host turns debugging on (executeOp hostOptions.debug, SnapshotSessionHost debug adapter, GameSession debugEnabled), and seat-view debug ops answer only for the asking seat (#481).

The seeded RNG is now ChaCha20 keyed by SHA-256 of the whole seed (#483), replacing mulberry32 on a 32-bit fold of it: every seed deals a different game from before, snapshot.randomState and action-checkpoint randomState are now a string ("chacha20:<key>:<position>") instead of a number, and setRandomState refuses a numeric state, so a game saved on an earlier engine cannot be continued after re-vendoring. The payload fingerprint now also covers the stored random state and the draws it gives. A game, session, MCTS bot or dev-host table started without a seed now gets a 128-bit seed from crypto.getRandomValues instead of Math.random, a non-string seed is refused, and randomState is required on snapshots and checkpoints.

selectGameOptions now refuses a number game option outside its declared min/max or off its step (counted from min, or 0), naming the option and its allowed range; a game declaring a non-finite bound, min above max, a non-positive step, or a default its own bounds refuse is refused when loaded. Re-vendor so a host cannot start a game with, say, rounds: 1000 against max: 10.

No BoardSmith host pushes a seat a state identical to the last one it sent (#487). SnapshotSessionHost's broadcast adapter is replaced by record (every view of record, spectator included, after each change) and push (only the seats whose view changed; seat 0 is the spectators), and it gains rosterChanged(), to call when a seat passes between a person and the bot; restoreFrom takes the views pages hold (playerViews, spectatorView) as given, so a roster change made while the host slept is pushed. GameSession's SessionInfo requires a connectionId. StatePushGate is exported from boardsmith/session and boardsmith/session-host. Animation event ids in a seat's payload now count only the events that seat may see (#489): a seat's state.animationEvents carries only its own events, numbered in its own sequence, seat views no longer carry animationEventSeq, every PlayerGameState names the seat it was built for (viewerSeat, 0 for a spectator) so a page that changes seat restarts its animation watermark, and animateTo refuses seat 0.

World element ids are now opaque (#482): Speck48/96 of the world's creation counter under a 96-bit key the HOST mints once when it creates a world (mintWorldElementIdKey from boardsmith/world, 24 hex digits), stores with the world beside nextElementId, and passes on every wake as createWorld's required elementIdKey (a world game built directly needs GameOptions.elementIdKey); never sent to a client. New platform-owned refusals: element-id-key-invalid (no key, or not 24 lowercase hex digits; the engine never mints a world key and never repeats a refused key) and element-id-key-mismatch (a stored partition does not hang from the root this key mints, raised before adoption). Ids are whole numbers below 2^48. nextElementId stays a counter value, never an id; worldIdAllocationOf(records, elementIdKey) now takes the key and whole StoredPartition records ({ parentId, json }, not bare json) and refuses records minted under another key; adopting a partition no longer spends counter values. Hidden-zone placeholder ids are now counted down from -1 per projection, for tables and worlds alike. Format break: the world format corpus is regenerated and records its key; worlds stored with sequential ids cannot be read by this engine, keep them on their archived runner or reset them. The pre-floor id lift (rekey exports, WorldStore.rekey, WorldStartOutcome.lifted) is removed; WorldStore gains elementIdKey(); createMemoryWorldStore takes the key first; TestWorld takes an optional elementIdKey.

SnapshotHostState carries the game's outcome (#490): durableState() and the persist adapter now hand out isComplete and winners beside snapshot, flowState and pendingStates, and restoreFrom requires both, so a host restored from a finished game publishes it as finished (with its winners, or as a draw) on broadcastCurrent() or rosterChanged() instead of as running. restoreFrom refuses a state missing either, or winners that are not seats of the table, and takes back anything durableState() returns, including winners with isComplete false (game.finish() inside a loop that does not stop on it). Re-vendor and store the whole persisted value, including the two new fields.

A finished game now ends the flow wherever it is: game.finish(), the END_GAME command, or the game's own isFinished() override (which now ends the flow even when the flow's isComplete differs) stops every construct (eachPlayer, loop, sequence, repeat, forEach, phase, simultaneous steps, turnLoop, stateAwareLoop), so op results report isComplete: true with winners and no seat is offered an action or follow-up. A node placed after the main loop no longer runs once an action calls finish(), including in turnLoop and stateAwareLoop. A pending multi-step action completes only when the flow offers it to that seat (refused with 'The game is finished.' or 'It's not your turn.' before anything runs), and undo on a finished game is refused as 'the game is finished'. Follow-ups are per seat and hold their seat (#494): FlowState.followUp is replaced by FlowState.followUps (one per seat, each with its seat, kept in the step's frame data so checkpoints, snapshots and undo carry them), followUpForSeat(flowState, seat) is the one check, and no other seat may take a seat's follow-up ('<action>' is not one of your actions right now.) or is offered it. While a seat holds a follow-up an actionStep keeps the turn with it and a simultaneousActionStep does not mark it done. By ruling, two things end a hold anyway: a game's custom allDone ends the step and drops the follow-ups it held (the one exception inside the step), and time limits always win: a host closes a timed step with a new host-only op, { type: 'expireTimedSeat', player, idleAction, args, boundaryKey }, one per seat still due (the action op has no timeout flag any more): it runs the idle action as the seat's own action when the step offers it, and otherwise drops a held seat's follow-up and ends its part (GameRunner.closeExpiredHeldSeat), recording that in actionHistory as a seat expiry ({ kind: 'seatExpiry', player, undoable: false }; actionHistory and GameStateSnapshot.actionHistory are now HistoryEntry[], SerializedAction | SerializedSeatExpiry, with isSeatExpiry to tell them apart) so GameRunner.replay re-applies it and undo counts it but never reaches behind it. The platform must compose expireTimedSeat itself from its round timer, never from a client message (no wire op maps to it), carry it through every op allowlist on its submission path (the builders table, the executor's validation schema, OP_BUILDERS), and stamp it with the key the timer was armed under: it is refused as stale like any submission, and refused outright on a step with no time limit. The seat drops its follow-up only by taking another action the step offers, and a refused action leaves it held. A held follow-up runs with its published args and without its condition, pick by pick or as one whole action (performAction/resume accept it for its owner; Game.performAction takes { asFollowUp }), enumerateLegalMoves and MCTSBot include its moves, a pending action completed in a simultaneous step is settled for its seat like a whole one (the step is no longer re-entered), dueSeats counts a held seat with no listed actions, and development builds warn when a held follow-up has no valid choice. A seat's own player state now carries the follow-up it holds (PlayerGameState.followUp, with metadata), and the table wiring starts it when no action is in progress (useActionController's heldFollowUp option), so a page reloaded mid-chain resumes it; a cancelled one stays startable from an Action Panel button (data-bs-follow-up) or the controller's resumeFollowUp(). FlowState.moveCount now counts every action in a turn-based step, each link of a follow-up chain included, so undo to the turn start reaches back over a whole chain (#495); move limits still count a chain once, and TurnRun gains actions beside count. offerFollowUp is now offerFollowUp(game, flowState, seat); Game.continueFlowAfterPendingAction and FlowEngine.resumeAfterExternalAction take the acting seat.

A multi-step action taken pick by pick is now gated by its condition (#493), decided in one place, GameRunner.refusalToPick(action, seat, pending), which the runner, PendingActionManager (GameSession) and the stateless selectionStep op all ask before a pick. The first pick is refused when the condition does not hold ("'<action>' is not available to you right now: '<label>' does not hold."); a later pick, including the one that completes the action, is refused when the condition held right after the seat's own previous pick and does not hold now, so another seat's move took it away ("'<action>' is no longer available to you: the game changed since your last choice, and '<label>' no longer holds."), with nothing run or recorded and the pending action left open. An action whose own picks (a repeat's onEach) end its condition still completes, and a held follow-up's condition is never checked. PendingActionState and SerializedPendingActionState gain conditionHeld?: boolean, which the platform's persisted pendingStates must carry through unchanged; a pending state persisted without it is treated as starting the action, so its condition must hold at its next pick.

The host-only seat close is renamed from expireTimedSeat to expireSeat, with the same inputs { type: 'expireSeat', player, idleAction, args, boundaryKey }, and it now works on any step, not only one that declares a time limit (#494 ruling: any host deadline closes a held seat the way a step timeout does): it runs the idle action as the seat's own action when the step offers it, otherwise drops the seat's held follow-up and ends its part (the turn passes, or the seat is marked done), recorded as the existing seatExpiry history entry so replay agrees. It is refused only when the seat can take neither, or as stale by its boundaryKey. The platform must use the name expireSeat, not expireTimedSeat (which its unmerged branch still uses), everywhere it builds or allowlists the op (the builders table, the executor's validation schema, OP_BUILDERS), still compose it only from its own timers and never from a client message, and may now submit it from any host deadline (such as a table's round deadline) on an untimed step, instead of failing the round when a seat holds a follow-up.

boardsmith/world exports the two steps every world host runs: runDueOccurrences, the occurrence loop for a due event, which answers resumeDue at the occurrence that refused (so a refused catch-up never re-runs what already ran, #538) and nextDue on success; and dispatchStep, the dispatch order (declaration walk, ONE schedule allowance read, apply, plan). ResidentWorld uses both; the platform should replace its own copies with them and read the allowance once (ShufflewickPub #569). The barrel is now an explicit list: 21 in-package helpers are no longer public (bindWorldFacilities, worldFacilitiesOf, assertCandidateBudget, readOnlyProjection, unkeyedScheduleRefusal, keyedScheduleRefusal, scheduleBatchRefusal, worldQueueRefusal, createInlinedPartitionStore, createWorldRunner, worldVacateByClockAction, worldNoticesPerSeat, WORLD_ORDERINGS, NOTICE_SCOPE, stampNotice, boxFull, MAX_ORDER_ID_LENGTH, assertWorldMigration, declaredSources, assertCreatedRoots, assertAnsweredAllocations); none has a platform caller (#539). A stale id allocation stamp is no longer repaired: once allocation-stale is raised the runner refuses every game-touching call with it, so the world stops and the host defect stays visible; the platform should drop its own repair (#540, ShufflewickPub #575).

SnapshotSessionHost's durable state is stored once (#536) and its calls cannot be made in the wrong order (#537). GameStateSnapshot (and each ActionCheckpoint) now records winners, the seats game.getWinners() named; SnapshotHostState is just { snapshot, pendingStates }, and the flow state, isComplete and winners are read from the snapshot through the new flowStateOf, isCompleteOf and winnersOf exports of boardsmith/session-host, so the platform drops flowState, isComplete and winners from its persisted payload. restoreFrom and the follow-up broadcastCurrent are replaced by the static SnapshotSessionHost.restore(adapters, { snapshot, pendingStates, botSeats, playerViews?, spectatorView? }) (botSeats required, [] when no bot plays), which refuses a snapshot without its flow state or winners and publishes once itself. The host applies the same check to every op result, so a game built on an engine before r131 is refused loudly instead of a won game being published as a draw. The adapters' live botSeats getter and rosterChanged() are replaced by host.setBotSeats(seats), which the platform calls before start() and whenever its roster or anything a derived roster depends on changes (it may be called from record); it publishes only when hasBotPlayers flips. PublishMeta gains cause: 'change' | 'republish' | 'restore' | 'roster', so the platform's own republishing flag can go: do per-change bookkeeping only for 'change'. Games must be built on this revision (r131) or later, because the host reads winners from the snapshot the bundle returns. createPlayerView reports availableActions: [] for a seat that cannot act (#498).

Op contract (BoardSmith #530, #535, #527, #536 step 5). (1) Op is now ExecutorOp | DevOp | HostOp; executeOp takes ExecutorOp | DevOp only, and boardsmith/session exports parseExecutorOp(value) -> { ok, op } | { ok: false, error }: strict, refuses unknown keys, requires boundaryKey on action/expireSeat/selectionStep. The executor should send the op as one field and validate it with parseExecutorOp instead of its own valibot schemas and request-to-op translator (ShufflewickPub #558). (2) OpResult is a union per op (OpResultFor<T>): every refusal is OpFailure { success: false, error, errorCode?, category, botPlayer? } with no snapshot, flowState, playerViews, isComplete or winners; every op that runs the game returns StateEnvelope { snapshot, playerViews, spectatorView, flowDebugInfo, persistCommit }; a resolveChoices success has only its answer fields; pendingState is on selectionStep results only. The top-level flowState, isComplete and winners are gone from every result: read snapshot.flowState and snapshot.winners (or flowStateOf/isCompleteOf/winnersOf from boardsmith/session-host); share OpResultFor instead of OpResult & ActionReturnValue casts. (3) A stale submission is refused with errorCode STALE_SUBMISSION: test for the code, never the message, and stop inferring staleness from boundary keys in game-session.ts (ShufflewickPub #560; the executor must forward errorCode). (4) No player or spectator view carries the reserved persist or persistPrivate attributes any more; every state-changing result carries persistCommit { public?, private? } read off the game root, and readPersistCommit(commit) and PersistenceStore.commit({ commit }) take it. takePrivateCommit and PrivateChannelCarrier are deleted: delete executor/src/persist-private.ts and its conformance test, and commit result.persistCommit at game over instead of digging it out of the last spectator view (ShufflewickPub #556).

Two changes the platform must run. (1) MCTS bot (#522): search moves are made for the seat they were listed for, and a step held open by allDone scores as a leaf; no fingerprint moves, so only this revision carries the fix to the platform. (2) GameShell runs only inside a host iframe (#515, #525): its gameType, displayName, playerCount, apiUrl and defaultBotPlayers props are removed (a game passes only :uis; a template that still passes them is not a type error, the values just fall through as unused attributes, so games should delete them), opened directly it shows one 'runs inside a host' sentence, and the HTTP client, matchmaking, GameLobby, WaitingRoom, GameHeader and HamburgerMenu are gone from boardsmith/client and boardsmith/ui. The controls menu no longer offers 'Leave game' (the host page owns leaving). In dev builds GameShell adds a dev-only Auto UI entry itself; games drop it from uis.ts. The Debug panel draws one seat button per seat in the state's players, numbered as the host numbers seats. The postMessage protocol between GameShell and its host is unchanged, and bundles already built carry their own shell.

boardsmith/session no longer exports the stateful GameSession or BotController (nor the types only they used: GameSessionOptions, SessionActionResult, UndoResult, ReadOnlyRunnerFacade, StoredGameState, StorageAdapter, BroadcastAdapter, SessionInfo, StateUpdate, LobbyUpdate, ActionRequest, UpdateNameRequest, GameConfig, BotSeatConfig); no host ran them, every host runs SnapshotSessionHost over executeOp. createHeadlessSession gains playerState(seat), readGame(), arrange(edit), and playerNames, options and teachingDisabled table options, and is the harness game tests use. ElementDiff is now exported from the session ops and types the debugStateDiff result; resolveChoices and debugHistory results name their choice, element and history entry types. No change to snapshots, views or ops.

An unbounded multiSelect ({ min: 1 } with no max) now reaches the wire with max ABSENT on a table as well as a world, in buildActionMetadata, Game#getActionSpace and the pick answer. Before, a table sent max: Infinity, which JSON turns into null, and the action panel read null as a cap of nothing (BoardSmith #508, ShufflewickPub #378). No fingerprint sees this: the fixtures carry no unbounded multiSelect. The platform must run this build for a table's unbounded picks to stop arriving with max: null.

The command undo system is gone (#499): 'boardsmith' no longer exports executeCommand, undoCommand, createInverseCommand or ActionExecutor (nor GameCommand, CommandResult, the *Command types, TrackOwner, VisibilityConfig or TrackCommandEmitter); Game loses execute(), commandHistory, undoLastCommand(), undoCommands(), replayCommands() and getElementClass(); GameElement loses setVisibilityInternal(); Track loses setCommandEmitter(), addInternal() and removeLastInternal(); Game.pushAnimationEvent() and Game.addMessageInternal() are now private. The debug ops are unchanged. No change to snapshots, views or ops. A polyhedral-potions rules.js built before its bs499 commit calls Track.setCommandEmitter and must be rebuilt.

A game starts once: a second Game.startFlow() (or GameRunner.start / TestGame.start) is refused with a readable error instead of re-running the flow's setup and opening execute nodes (#502); the startTutorial op now hands the turn back to the flow's first seat through the new Game.restartFlowForTutorial(), which re-runs neither the flow's setup nor its opening execute nodes, so a tutorial opened during the opponent's turn no longer leaves the learner with no action, and the op is refused when the restarted flow would not prompt the requesting seat (#546).

A simultaneous step now decides a seat that has just acted the same way it decides every seat at entry and on refreshAwaitingActions (#501): a seat skipPlayer now excludes leaves awaitingPlayers at once (and the step completes if it was the last seat) instead of staying prompted, and a function-valued actions list that returns an unregistered name after a seat acts halts the flow with the 'references unknown action' error instead of silently dropping the name. FlowEngine gains the private helpers offeredActions, seatEligibility, offeredSequentialActions and offeredSimultaneousActions, which is the surface change; each seat's available actions are now read once per evaluation rather than once per declared name.
